correctness.rationale: Write an even prefix-normal palindrome as x x^R and insert a central zero. For factors of length at most |x|, factors avoiding the new zero are inherited, while a crossing factor loses only a zero and becomes a length-(k-1) factor of the original word that can be extended to length k. For longer factors, every factor crosses the center; deleting the zero gives a factor one shorter, and the new prefix similarly reduces to the old prefix one shorter. Prefix normality transfers in both regimes. Deleting the center proves injectivity, and the all-one odd palindrome proves strictness. Exhaustive replay through length 23 agrees.
